classification.difficultyReason: Requires solving a parameterised inequality and relating its interval endpoints to a prescribed length.

content.prompt: Find the value(s) of $t$ such that the solution to the inequality $\dfrac{2x+t}{x+1}\leq1$ is an interval of length 3 units.

answer.short:
$t=-1$ or $t=5$.

After multiplying by $(x+1)^2$, the interval endpoints are $-1$ and $1-t$, so its length is $|2-t|$.
answer.worked:
The domain excludes $x=-1$. Multiply by $(x+1)^2>0$ on this domain.

$$\begin{align*}(2x+t)(x+1)&\leq(x+1)^2\\(2x+t)(x+1)-(x+1)^2&\leq0\\(x+t-1)(x+1)&\leq0\end{align*}$$

For $t<2$, the solution is $-1<x\leq1-t$, with length $2-t$.

For $t>2$, the solution is $1-t\leq x<-1$, with length $t-2$.

For $t=2$, the only polynomial candidate is the excluded value $x=-1$, so the solution set is empty.

$$\begin{align*}|2-t|&=3\\2-t&=3\quad\text{or}\quad2-t=-3\\t&=-1\quad\text{or}\quad t=5\end{align*}$$
